Scholarship

Post Matric Scholarship (PMS) — apply & check status

The Bihar Government’s Post Matric Scholarship (PMS) supports SC, ST, BC and EBC students studying after Class 10. Applications and status checks happen only on the official state portals — pick your category’s portal and keep your Aadhaar number and registered mobile number ready.

BC / EBC students: pmsonline.bihar.gov.in · SC / ST students: scstpmsonline.bihar.gov.in · Payment status can also be tracked on PFMS (pfms.nic.in)
  1. Open your category’s official portal from the buttons here
  2. Log in with your User ID, or open “Application Status”
  3. Enter your Aadhaar / registration details and mobile number
  4. View your application status, verification stage and payment details

About the University

A citadel of learning in the land of enlightenment

Magadh University was established on 1 March 1962 under the Magadh University Act, 1961, and began functioning the following day. It owes its founding to Satyendra Narayan Sinha, the then Education Minister of Bihar, while the foundation of the university was laid by Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, the then President of India. The renowned historian K. K. Dutta served as its founder Vice-Chancellor.

The university started with two constituent colleges, 32 affiliated colleges and seven postgraduate departments. It has since grown into the largest university of Bihar, and is today governed by the Bihar State University Act, 1976. Its jurisdiction spans the five districts of Gaya, Aurangabad, Nawada, Jehanabad and Arwal, and its secular, disciplined campus draws students from across India and abroad every year.

  • Founded1 March 1962 · Founder — Satyendra Narayan Sinha
  • First Vice-ChancellorProf. K. K. Dutta, eminent historian
  • RecognitionUniversity Grants Commission (UGC) · NAAC accredited

Campus Life

Life on a 460-acre green campus

Mannulal Central Library

A multi-storeyed central library holding around 1,62,000 books, manuscripts and reading material, alongside departmental libraries and national and international journals.

Hostels

Eight hostels on campus accommodate around 1,500 students, including a dedicated girls' hostel for 150 residents.

Laboratories & Research

All science departments — including Psychology and Geography — maintain well-equipped laboratories with modern instruments for teaching and research.

Seminars & Scholars

State and national level seminars are organised regularly across faculties, and the campus welcomes international students every year.

The Bodh Gaya Setting

Studying where the Buddha found enlightenment

The university stands at Bodh Gaya, a short distance from the Mahabodhi Temple and the Bodhi Tree under which Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment. Few universities in the world teach within sight of such a civilisational landmark — a setting that shapes the university's strength in Buddhist Studies, Pali & Prakrit, philosophy and the humanities, and gives its campus its distinctive, contemplative character.

Admissions

How to apply

Admission to university departments and colleges follows the notifications published on the official portal each academic session.

1

Check the Notice

Find the admission notification for your course on the official website.

2

Apply Online

Fill the application form and upload documents on the admission portal.

3

Merit / Entrance

Selection is by merit list or entrance test (such as the Ph.D. Admission Test), as notified.

4

Verification

Attend counselling with original documents at the department or college.

5

Enrolment

Pay the fee, complete enrolment and collect your registration number.

Note: Admission schedules, fees and seat details change every session. Always confirm the latest dates and eligibility on the official university website before applying.

Getting Here

  • By Air: Gaya International Airport, about 13 km from Bodh Gaya, with the larger hub at Patna.
  • By Rail: Gaya Junction is the nearest major railway station, well connected to Patna, Delhi and Kolkata.
  • By Road: Bodh Gaya lies on the Gaya–Rajgir road, around 110 km south of Patna.
